name: Romiplostim
route_note: SC injection once weekly, dose adjusted to platelet count

discovery.note: A 'peptibody': an IgG1 Fc fragment carrying two copies of a TPO-mimetic peptide with no sequence homology to TPO, avoiding the antibody problems of earlier recombinant TPO. Year is the priority date of Amgen's patent application on dimeric thrombopoietin peptide mimetics (WO 00/24770).

tagline: Weekly Fc-peptide fusion that stimulates the thrombopoietin receptor
summary: Romiplostim is an Fc–peptide fusion protein that binds and activates the thrombopoietin receptor, increasing platelet production. It is given by weekly injection for chronic immune thrombocytopenia and was later approved for haematopoietic acute radiation syndrome.
mechanism: Romiplostim binds the thrombopoietin receptor (MPL) at the same site as endogenous TPO and activates JAK2–STAT signalling in megakaryocyte progenitors, increasing megakaryocyte number and platelet output.

Its TPO-mimetic peptides share no sequence with TPO, which avoids induction of neutralising antibodies that cross-react with native TPO, a problem that halted earlier pegylated recombinant megakaryocyte growth factor.
uses: Immune thrombocytopenia in adults and children with insufficient response to other therapy
Haematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation syndrome

history.title: TPO antibodies
history.detail: Development of pegylated recombinant MGDF stops after neutralising antibodies cause thrombocytopenia, prompting non-homologous agonists.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Nplate approved for chronic immune thrombocytopenia in adults.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Authorised in the EU for chronic ITP.

history.title: Paediatric ITP
history.detail: FDA extends use to children aged one year and older.

history.title: Radiation syndrome
history.detail: FDA approves romiplostim for haematopoietic acute radiation syndrome.

serious: progression to acute myeloid leukaemia in myelodysplastic syndromes
loss of response and rebound thrombocytopenia

facts: Nplate (August 2008) was the first thrombopoietin receptor agonist approved by the FDA, ahead of oral eltrombopag later that year.
In January 2021 the FDA approved romiplostim to increase survival after acute exposure to myelosuppressive doses of radiation (haematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation syndrome).
